intro: The fiftieth screen read 99 pictures, the set's 21 and 78 probes, with thirteen readers and four scorers: 1,084 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **All 64 templates pass the legibility gate**, where 63 did in v0.52. `square_wheel` reads 0.938 in its eight pictures, from 0.812: the four wheelbarrows read in full, twelve items of twelve, and what is left under full marks is a bicycle, whose square wheels one reader of four did not name. Of the 18 items under full marks, sixteen are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out, and two are that bicycle's. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. Twenty-four of the 99 pictures are v0.52's to the pixel, and their 289 items are a second reading: 282 have the score they had, four of the seven others are the clouds, and the other three are every item of v0.52's that was under full marks in those pictures and not a cloud, all three now in full with nothing drawn. The set's score is 0.984, for 0.986. On the strict count 56 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.52's 54. The four grown figures are called young first in 5 of their 81 pictures, for 5 of 85, three of the five the man in the red shirt reading.
design:
## Design tests

The two rules of revision 49 were read in five whole test scenes by five fresh readers, one picture each (`vision/design_tests_v053.md`). I looked at the five before any reader had them and found nothing to mend.
- **The larger wheel among other events:** named as the barrow's wheel, and square, in the barrow's own inventory line by all three readers who had one: "Its wheel is a black square with a cross inside instead of a circle."; "On the right, where the wheel should be, is a square black wheel with spokes."
- **The jump beside a game of catch,** under the first rule, a gap of 150 units: both readers still tied the jump to the game: "The jumping girl: could be cheering at a game, or jumping to try to catch the ball; she is not looking at the ball (eyes closed)." So the rule became the other kind, and the two are never planned together. That rule draws nothing a reader could be shown; the two pictures are the reason for it.
- **The jump alone:** "He has both arms raised, with his feet off the ground above his shadow, so he is jumping or cheering."
- **Every forced event was read,** fifteen of fifteen. One reader had a catcher in profile facing away from the ball; on a crop his face is toward it. It is on the watch list.

No picture was built again after a reading.
screen:
Across all 99 pictures 1,084 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.52: 1,095 of 1,114, none). Of the 18 under full marks:
- sixteen are setting items that four readers left out, fourteen the clouds and two a tree, all zeros (v0.52 had twelve, from four readers). One reader left the clouds out of six of its seven pictures;
- two are the square-wheeled bicycle's in the new tier-4 playground, a half mark and a zero: "- Red bicycle, right-front, standing on its kickstand." and, among the unsure things, "The bicycle has no rider; it is upright on a kickstand, slightly odd-looking but plausible."

The set's headline is all items 0.984 (0.986 in v0.52). Of its 286 items five are under full marks: the clouds in three pictures (things 0.972) and the bicycle's two (contradictions 0.946). Actions and inferences read 1.00.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.54 is `vision/flaws_v053.md`.

**The square wheel.** Eight pictures, four of the wheelbarrow and four of the bicycle. The four barrows read in full, twelve items of twelve, where two of v0.52's four went unnoticed: "The wheelbarrow wheel is square rather than round, which looks unintentionally strange."; "The wheelbarrow's wheel is square, which looks impossible or like a deliberate joke." Three of the four are the pictures of v0.52's screen with the wheel larger and nothing else moved. One has the second reading that the bench found: "It could alternatively be a separate square object (a grate or frame) standing in front of the wheelbarrow." The bicycle, whose wheels are as v0.52 drew them, reads in full in three pictures and is the one miss in the fourth. What the barrow's wheel was to v0.52's readers, a bicycle's can be to v0.53's, and the bicycle is first on the next list.

**A second reading of the pictures that came back.** Twenty-four of the 99 pictures are v0.52's to the pixel, nineteen of the set and five probes, and they hold 289 items. Item for item against v0.52's screen, 282 have the same score, four are higher and three lower. Four of the seven are the clouds. The other three went up, and are every item of v0.52's that was under full marks in these pictures and not a setting item: the bread for the ducks, the thief bird's inference in the tier-4 street and the square-wheeled bicycle of the tier-3 street. Nothing was drawn for any of them. A pass or a miss on one reader's sentence is the size of what a screen can show.

**The cast in the descriptions.** The cast is v0.52's, so this is a second count of the same figures. By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the four grown figures of v0.49's count are called by a young name first in 5 of their 81 pictures, for 5 of 85 in v0.52: the woman in purple in 2 of 25, the woman in the yellow dress in none of 21, the man in the red shirt in 3 of 19 and the man in green in none of 16. All three of the man's are a man reading, twice on a bench and once as he walks: "Boy on bench, front right: brown hair, red shirt, blue trousers, reading a red book." The five are four readers' of thirteen. The beard of the man in green is in his line in 9 of his 16 pictures (16 of 25 in v0.52), and the moustache of the man in the red shirt in 1 of 19 (3 of 12).

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers listed 79 full marks as judgement calls, for 67 in v0.52. In 32 the target stands beside another reading (34 in v0.52), and in 47 a near word or a target partly said was credited (33), thirty of them a word for a person. With the 32 halved, eight templates are under 0.9, and 56 of the 64 pass (54 in v0.52): the wave (0.833, on three items), the begging dog (0.861), the stopped hose and the kite in the tree (0.875 each), and the stalking cat, the floating box, the upward water and the blown hat (0.889 each). With all 79 halved, 44 pass (43). The four scorers listed 20, 20, 17 and 22 calls, so the strict counts compare only roughly.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 30 oddities in the 99 pictures, 0.3 a picture for v0.52's 0.2, and 7 of them in the set for 4. The readers' remarks were 2.62 per picture (2.46). What the oddities are about: figures over the pond's near edge, in four pictures; the heavy seesaw's man and the plank between his legs, in two; swept leaves with no tree near them, in two; and a goat in a park, in two.
redrawn: One thing a template draws was changed, the wheelbarrow's square wheel. `square_wheel`, 0.812 and under the gate in v0.52, reads 0.938 in eight pictures: its four barrows in full, and one bicycle of four missed. `jump` and `play_catch`, which are no longer planned into one picture, read 1.00 in five pictures each. `bird_steals` and `ducks_bread`, 0.944 and 0.967 in v0.52, read 1.00 with nothing drawn for either: passes their drawings did not earn. `dog_begs` and `blocked_hose` read 1.00 and are the two with the most full marks beside another reading, five each; `wave`, `kite_in_tree`, `cat_stalks_bird`, `floating_box`, `water_upward` and `windy_hat` read 1.00 and fall under 0.9 on the strict count. It is one screen, of 3 to 24 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.17.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (33 in three, 8 in four, 16 in five, 2 in six, and one each in seven, eight, ten, thirteen and sixteen). 64 of 64 pass, where 63 did in v0.52, 64 in v0.51 and 62 in v0.50. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. One template is under 1.00: `square_wheel` (0.938 on twenty-four items in eight pictures, no misread); the other 63 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v053/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 32 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 56 of the 64 pass. The square wheel's pass is the larger wheel's and one reader's: the four barrows read in full with the wheel larger, and an unchanged bicycle that had a half mark in v0.52 read in full. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: Six of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where five had in v0.52, and all six are the square wheel's: its two contradiction items' mean, spread and salience, the salience from -0.022 to 0.036 with the larger wheel. Nothing else moved, as the cast is v0.52's. The planner drew v0.52's set again in fourteen cells of sixteen. The calibration was measured once, with the rules as they are released (`tools/cycle/calib_cmp.py`).
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 49. The twelve cells of tiers 1 to 3 placed on their showcase seeds, the tier-4 park on the v0.43 seed and the tier-4 street on v0.49's, on its twenty-second step, each with v0.52's templates and v0.52's people in v0.52's places; all fourteen, and the five isomorphs built from them, are v0.52's pictures to the pixel. The tier-4 playground did not place on v0.52's base or on six more, and placed on the eighth base of the search, on its seventh step. The tier-4 garden of v0.52 held a jump beside a game of catch; the free search failed on ten bases, and the cell is v0.46's garden set forced on v0.46's seed, the one of four earlier sets that placed under revision 49 (`tools/cycle/forced_cell.py`). The probe pass built 61 and left one template short, the begging dog; two small forced groups filled it, the pass stratified by angle added 12, and three more were forced for the wheelbarrow (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 78 probes, 47 gardens, 23 parks, 6 playgrounds and 2 streets. Twenty-four of the 99 pictures are v0.52's to the pixel. **I looked at the other 75 on sheets before any reader had them, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 99 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 355 of 355. Its soft palette warning is raised by 314 records (342 of 388 in v0.52), with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
